auditor: Independent galois_audit agent, with separately delegated finite spot checks
primary_verdict: proved as written within the exact reviewed scope, using explicitly verified external theorem inputs
verdict_scope: Conjunction of the current closed elementary field examples, universal regular-operator statements, typed field/module translations, scoped conditional arithmetic implications, finite embedding and certificate results. This is not a verdict proving the unrestricted inverse or regular inverse Galois problem.
strongest_safe_statement: Every finite group has a faithful rational regular module and a faithful field action on Q(x_g); Artin realizes it over the invariant base, and the subgroup calculus is exact in the regular realization. The five named groups are realized over Q. The stated rationality, regular-family, continuous proper-lift and explicit field-certificate inputs imply their scoped arithmetic conclusions.
remaining_implication: Supply a verified arithmetic witness for every prescribed finite G: the certificate data or one of the declared conditional route inputs. The present sources do not supply that uniformly.
cheapest_next_exact_check: For any proposed individual field certificate, check irreducibility, all root/composition remainders in the stated reversed substitution order, and pairwise distinct residues. This audits a candidate; it does not assert candidate existence.

normalized_claim_cards.title: Polynomial formulation
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: Finite Galois realizations over Q are equivalent to separable-polynomial splitting-field realizations.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: An actual finite Galois L/Q in the reverse direction.
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: Automorphisms fix Q and act on all roots.
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: Primitive element generates all L; normality supplies every conjugate, so its splitting field equals L. Root action is faithful; irreducible root action is transitive by extension of embeddings.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: Only the stated hypotheses and conclusion.

normalized_claim_cards.title: Regular module
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: Every finite G has an injective group-algebra action on its left regular module.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: G finite; V=C[G] with declared basis delta_g.
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: lambda(a)delta_g=delta_ag; compositions from right to left.
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: The action law makes the linear extension an algebra homomorphism. Applying a linear combination to delta_1 recovers every coefficient.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: Group faithfulness alone is weaker than injectivity of the group algebra action. Trivial G is included.

normalized_claim_cards.title: Quadratic realization
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: Q(sqrt2)/Q has full group C2 and fixed field Q.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: Irreducible X^2-2.
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: a+b sqrt2 maps to a-b sqrt2.
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: Parity descent proves nonsquare; conjugation preserves the defining relation; two possible root images exhaust automorphisms; fixed coefficients are rational.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: The stated generalization requires d in Q^times to be nonsquare.

normalized_claim_cards.title: Biquadratic realization
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: Q(sqrt2,sqrt3)/Q has group V4 and exactly the three named quadratic fixed fields.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: sqrt3 not in Q(sqrt2), checked by coefficient comparison.
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: Independent signs; s changes sqrt2 and t changes sqrt3.
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: Degree tower is 2*2; all four signs preserve the relations and exhaust degree4. The displayed rational basis gives the three fixed fields directly.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: Only the stated hypotheses and conclusion.

normalized_claim_cards.title: Cyclic cubic realization
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: X^3+X^2-2X-1 has splitting field Q(alpha), degree3 and group C3.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: Rational roots +/-1 excluded; discriminant49 is nonzero.
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: alpha -> alpha^2-2 -> 1-alpha-alpha^2 -> alpha.
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: Reduced identities give sum -1, pair sum -2, product1 and the root-cycle identities. Irreducibility gives degree3 and the displayed root field splits the polynomial. The Vandermonde cross check uses V^2=49 and characteristic not2.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: Direct root proof is primary. Square-discriminant criterion is used only over Q; no characteristic2 extension of the source wording is accepted.

normalized_claim_cards.title: S3 realization
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: The splitting field of X^3-2 has degree6 and full group S3.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: Irreducible cubic; real root alpha; primitive cube root zeta.
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: tau(alpha)=zeta alpha, tau(zeta)=zeta; complex conjugation inverts tau.
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: Real Q(alpha) excludes zeta; its quadratic equation doubles degree3. Faithful action on three roots and order6 identify the full group.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: A single real root field has degree3 and is not the splitting field.

normalized_claim_cards.title: S4 realization
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: X^4-X-1 has full splitting-field group S4.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: Monic integral polynomial; squarefree reductions at2 and7.
normalized_claim_cards.coefficient_domain: Q; exact F2 and F7 checks
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: Cycle types4 and3+1 in the actual root action; no joint canonical labelling.
normalized_claim_cards.evidence_kind: specific written field example plus checked external bridge
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: Mod2 has no linear factor and no factor X^2+X+1. Mod7 cubic residues are [5,4,1,2,6,5,5]; derivative and value at3 prove squarefreeness. LC08 supplies order4/order3 elements. Order12 would be the unique index2 subgroup A4, impossible because a four-cycle is odd.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: Finite modular factorization does not independently prove the Frobenius bridge. Only cycle shape, not a chosen permutation, follows.

normalized_claim_cards.title: Variable action and fixed field
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: For every finite G, E=Q(x_g) over K=E^G is finite Galois with full group G and degree |G|.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: Algebraically independent variables indexed by G; actual field action.
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: sigma_h(x_g)=x_hg is a faithful left action.
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: Permutation extends from polynomial ring to fractions, inverse sigma_h^-1; x_1 detects faithfulness. Artin applies to the actual finite subgroup of field automorphisms.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: K changes with G. For trivial G, E=K=Q(x_1), whereas its arithmetic realization is Q.

normalized_claim_cards.title: Primitive generic element and constants
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: E=K(x_1), trdeg_Q(K)=|G|, and Q is algebraically closed in Q(x_g).
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: Same independent-variable field; rational denominator nonzero.
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: Orbit labels are distinct; invariants have action-fixed coefficients.
normalized_claim_cards.source_locator: paper/chapters01_03.tex: eq:g03-orbit-polynomial, eq:g03-transdegree, A sufficient rationality route
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: A minimal polynomial vanishing at x_1 vanishes at all |G| roots and therefore has degree |G|. Algebraicity preserves transcendence degree. Sum invariant is transcendental by substitution. For an algebraic rational function A/B, evaluate at a rational tuple with B nonzero: the irreducible minimal polynomial acquires a rational root and has degree1.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: Transcendence degree does not prove pure transcendence of the invariant field. Orbit polynomials for arbitrary elements may repeat roots.

normalized_claim_cards.title: Conditional Noether route
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: An actual rational presentation K=Q(t_1,...,t_d) for this invariant field implies a G realization over Q.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: Displayed t_i algebraically independent and generating all K; d=|G|>=1.
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: Transport the finite field extension across the rational-base presentation.
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: C08 gives finite Galois/full G; C09 gives constants Q; the full primitive-extension Hilbert contract applies outside the nonzero constraints.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: No rationality hypothesis is supplied uniformly; no necessity or equivalence with inverse Galois is proved. Swan negative context is source-attributed only and not a dependency.

normalized_claim_cards.title: Two-variable invariant specialization
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: For the swap action, Q(x,y)^C2=Q(s,p), s=x+y,p=xy; the named three specializations have the stated outcomes.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: Independent x,y; exchange fixes s,p and does not fix x.
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: Swap of variables; inclusion reverses fixed-field conditions.
normalized_claim_cards.evidence_kind: specific written field and specialization example
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: Root polynomial bounds degree by2; nonfixed x gives degree2, so Artin identifies the fixed field. Algebraic extension gives independence of s,p. Values (0,-2),(0,-1),(2,1) give quadratic, split and repeated polynomials respectively.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: Nonzero discriminant is insufficient for retaining the group.

normalized_claim_cards.title: Subgroup projection and rank
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: E_H is the orthogonal projection onto V^H with rank [G:H]; H<=K gives E_HE_K=E_KE_H=E_K.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: G finite, H<=G, regular orthonormal basis.
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: Left H-orbits are right cosets Hg; subgroup order reverses range order.
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: Inversion proves adjoint equality; uniform H-product counts prove idempotence. Averaging fixes exactly the invariant range. Disjoint coset sums give an orthonormal basis of [G:H] vectors; nested projections give the products.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: Identity subgroup gives I; whole G gives rank1, including trivial G. Normalization would fail in characteristic dividing |H|.

normalized_claim_cards.title: Exact compatibility
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: In the regular realization, E_HE_K=E_KE_H iff HK=KH iff HK is a subgroup; then product is E_HK=E_<H,K>.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: H,K subgroups of finite G; injective group-algebra realization.
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: Ordered multiplication of averages retains product-set support.
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: Expressions h*k=x are in bijection with H intersect K, giving coefficient 1/|HK| on exactly HK. Algebra injectivity makes commuting operators equal supported algebra elements, hence HK=KH. Closure/inversion identify a subgroup and the generated subgroup. Fixed-range intersection equals V^<H,K> without permutability.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: Permutability does not mean elementwise commuting. A common fixed-range projection need not equal an ordered product.

normalized_claim_cards.title: Normality and quotient
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: Normality of H, centrality of e_H, commutation of E_H with all lambda(g), and invariance of V^H are equivalent; the quotient action is faithful.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: H<=G finite; regular unitary group-algebra-faithful realization.
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: Conjugation transports e_H to e_gHg^-1; normal quotient acts on right cosets.
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: Equality of conjugated supports gives normality. Injectivity gives operator equivalence. Unitarity and invariance under inverses make the orthogonal complement invariant. For normal H, the action is the regular G/H action; fixing the identity coset forces membership in H.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: Merely faithful group actions do not imply the converse; C16 is an exact counterexample.

normalized_claim_cards.title: S3 matrices
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: The declared six-by-six H12,H23 matrices and commutator are exact, with squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm3/4.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: Basis 1,(12),(23),(13),(123),(132); right-to-left permutation composition.
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: Left regular matrix columns are images of basis vectors.
normalized_claim_cards.evidence_kind: exact specific finite computation and written example
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: ab=(123), ba=(132); commutator at delta_1 is (delta_123-delta_132)/4. Each of six columns has two entries of magnitude1/4. Fresh incidence construction and exhaustive subset/pair checks match the JSON after its declared basis conversion.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: Finite completeness is six subgroups, all64 subsets tested, and all36 ordered subgroup pairs; not arbitrary finite groups.

normalized_claim_cards.title: Faithful S4 boundary
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: On the faithful sum-zero standard S4 module, a nonnormal four-cycle subgroup has zero average and commutes with a nonpermutable subgroup average.
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: Coordinate permutation action; its algebra action is not injective.
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: Faithfulness follows from W plus constant line giving the full permutation representation. Four-cycle average sends all vectors to the constant line, so restricts to0. krk=(1342) is not a power of r; kr belongs to KH but neither form r^i or r^ik in HK.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: Refutes only the overstrong group-faithful converse; it is not an inverse Galois counterexample.

normalized_claim_cards.title: Fixed-field lattice
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: For a given finite Galois L/Q, fixed fields have reverse inclusions, expected degrees and normal quotients; intersection and compositum correspond to generated subgroup and subgroup intersection.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: Actual finite Galois L/Q already supplied.
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: H maps contravariantly to L^H.
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: Fixed elements of both H,K are fixed by every generated word. Automorphisms fixing the compositum fix both fields and are exactly H intersect K. The external bijection identifies the resulting field.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: No permutability is needed for lattice identities; arithmetic existence is an input.

normalized_claim_cards.title: Normal-basis translation
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: An existing finite Galois L/Q is equivariantly isomorphic to Q[G] as a module, and subgroup averages transport.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: Normal basis generator alpha for existing L/Q.
normalized_claim_cards.coefficient_domain: Q; extension of scalars to C for orthogonal module chart
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: Phi(sum c_g g)=sum c_g g(alpha) is equivariant and linear.
normalized_claim_cards.source_locator: paper/chapters04_06.tex: eq:b-normal-basis-map; paper/chapters07_08.tex: The multiplication carried by a normal basis
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: Normal basis gives a rational vector-space isomorphism and group-action equivariance. Transported multiplication mu(u,v)=Phi^-1(Phi(u)Phi(v)) is rational bilinear, commutative, associative, unital, without zero divisors, and action preserving.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: Usual group algebra multiplication is not the field multiplication. Complexification is a module translation, not creation of a number field.

normalized_claim_cards.title: Trace and norm
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: P_H=Tr_(L/L^H)/|H|, norm is product of H-conjugates, and trace/norm obey tower composition; the quadratic loss example is exact.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: Actual finite Galois L/Q; H<=K<=G for the tower.
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: Embeddings of L^H over L^K are represented by left cosets kH in K/H.
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: LC13 provides separable sum/product and towers. For a+b sqrt2, average a, trace2a, norm a^2-2b^2. Values1 and1+sqrt2 have identical projected/trace data but different norms1,-1; P(sqrt2)^2 differs from P(2).
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: Norm is multiplicative and homogeneous of degree |H| over L^H, generally not additive. Embedding cosets kH differ from regular left-action orbits Hg.

normalized_claim_cards.title: One-parameter Hilbert implication
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: A verified finite Galois F/Q(t), modeled outside nonzero constraints, has infinitely many rational specializations with full group G; a regular input therefore suffices.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: Primitive polynomial for the entire F; actual field extension; Q Hilbertian; constraints include coefficients, denominators and discriminant.
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: Specialization group embeds in G and full primitive degree forces equality.
normalized_claim_cards.evidence_kind: checked external theorem and proved conditional implication
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: LC03 supplies full-degree irreducibility on a Zariski-dense Hilbert subset. In one parameter the polynomial exceptional set is finite. The corollary applies after the regular field is constructed.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: Regularity is not necessary for the broader specialization theorem as stated here. Infinite suitable values are not claimed to give infinitely many distinct fields for nonregular inputs. Several-parameter exclusions can be infinite hypersurfaces; characteristic zero alone is insufficient.

normalized_claim_cards.title: Nonregular cubic toy
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: X^3-t has generic S3 splitting field Q(u,zeta3), t=u^3, and specialized groups trivial,C2,S3 at0,1,2.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: t transcendental; generic polynomial Eisenstein at t.
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: Full root closure includes zeta3; over C(t) it is instead cyclic C3.
normalized_claim_cards.source_locator: paper/chapters04_06.tex: eq:b-cubic-family and A cubic toy that changes group
normalized_claim_cards.evidence_kind: specific written generic-field and finite specialization example
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: Root field Q(u) has only Q algebraic constants; a nonconstant rational function would make u algebraic over its own generated field. Thus zeta3 gives degree2 beyond degree3. It is an extra constant, proving nonregularity. Specific factorization/degree arguments give all three values.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: Not a worked regular input. The t=1 group drop is nonsingular; t=0 is a repeated-root degeneration.

normalized_claim_cards.title: Arithmetic quotient to field
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: A continuous finite-target lift of G_Q gives a finite Galois M/Q with group its image, containing the prescribed L; an onto lift gives E,N,G with the specified quotient.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: G_Q has Krull topology; finite E,G discrete; rho is continuous onto restriction for finite Galois L; pi lift equation.
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: ker(lift) subset ker(rho) reverses to L subset M.
normalized_claim_cards.source_locator: paper/chapters04_06.tex: eq:b-lift-equation and The diagram and its fields
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: Continuity makes the kernel open, homomorphism makes it normal. LC16 gives finite fixed field and quotient group; first isomorphism theorem gives image J. If image is E, restriction agrees with pi and its kernel is N.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: Abstract discontinuous maps are not arithmetic certificates. Weak image J may be proper in E.

normalized_claim_cards.title: Finite C2/C4 obstruction
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: The identity of finite C2 has no homomorphic lift through C4 parity.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: Domain is the finite group C2, not G_Q.
normalized_claim_cards.coefficient_domain: Z/2 and Z/4 in additive notation
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: Images must preserve the order2 relation and parity quotient.
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: A lift generator must be odd, but 2y=0 mod4 permits only y=0,2. The incompatible possibilities are exhausted.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: No arithmetic impossibility statement for G_Q follows from this finite-domain obstruction.

normalized_claim_cards.title: Split and diagonal weak lifts
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: A continuous split section composed with onto rho is weak; for nontrivial N that particular lift is not proper. Onto coordinates need not give an onto paired map.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: Section s is a homomorphism; finite discrete targets; continuous rho.
normalized_claim_cards.coefficient_domain: Finite groups and the stated topological domain
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: pi*s*rho=rho; split image s(G); diagonal C2 example.
normalized_claim_cards.source_locator: paper/chapters04_06.tex: ex:b-split-weak and A split lift can still be weak
normalized_claim_cards.evidence_kind: universal written implication with exact finite examples
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: s is continuous between finite discrete groups and rho is continuous by hypothesis. Split image order is |G|<|E| when N nontrivial. Both coordinate identity maps C2->C2 pair to a two-element diagonal in C2^2.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: An available section does not prove properness. For the finite C2 domain no onto map to a four-element target exists.

normalized_claim_cards.title: Kernel coverage
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: For any group Gamma and onto rho, a homomorphic lift is onto iff lift(ker rho)=N.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: Exact finite-target sequence; rho onto; compatible homomorphic lift.
normalized_claim_cards.coefficient_domain: Arbitrary groups; finite targets in application
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: Multiplication order e*lift(gamma)^-1 and delta*gamma is retained.
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: Forward preimages of n lie in ker rho. Conversely choose gamma over pi(e); coverage lifts e*lift(gamma)^-1 via delta in ker rho, giving e=lift(delta gamma).
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: Centrality is unnecessary. Continuity must additionally hold for the arithmetic application.

normalized_claim_cards.title: Central correction equation
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: For central N and normalized section s, c(g,h)=s(g)s(h)s(gh)^-1 is normalized and satisfies the displayed cocycle law; u*s*rho is a homomorphism precisely by the stated correction equation.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: N central in E; s(1)=1; rho a homomorphism; u takes values in N with u(1)=1.
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: u(gamma delta)=u(gamma)u(delta)c(rho gamma,rho delta).
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: Associativity plus centrality gives the cocycle identity. Multiplication of corrected sections gives the correction equation with the manuscript sign. For continuous rho, finite-discrete s*rho is continuous; both continuity directions follow by multiplying/inverting it. C4 has c(1,1)=2 and both u choices fail 0=2u+2 mod4.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: Noncentral kernels require an action and a changed equation. No arithmetic vanishing theorem is asserted; homomorphic weak correction still requires kernel coverage for properness.

normalized_claim_cards.title: Field certificate
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: For |G|=n, irreducible monic f degree n and n distinct compatible root substitutions in Q[X]/f imply full Galois group G over Q.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: Root remainder zero for each r_g; r_1=X modf; r_h(r_g)=r_gh modf; all residues distinct; actual quotient field.
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: sigma_g*sigma_h applies sigma_h first; hence polynomial substitution order r_h(r_g).
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: Root substitution is a unital field endomorphism, injective and finite-dimensional hence onto. Congruences give an injective G-action. Artin gives [L:L^Sigma]=n. Since [L:Q]=n, the tower forces L^Sigma=Q and the full group is Sigma.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: No certificate-existence claim for arbitrary G. n=1 is included. A reducible degree-n quotient does not satisfy the field input.

normalized_claim_cards.title: Certificate examples and format
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: The quadratic certificate closes C2, and any existing characteristic-zero realization can be encoded in the certificate format.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: f=X^2-2,r_1=X,r_s=-X for the example; existing finite Galois L/Q for general encoding.
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: Unique power-basis images encode field automorphisms.
normalized_claim_cards.source_locator: paper/chapters07_08.tex: An exact quadratic certificate and paragraph after thm:g07-certificate
normalized_claim_cards.evidence_kind: specific exact certificate plus conditional encoding
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: Quadratic root, composition and distinctness tests are immediate exact remainders. r_s=X fails distinctness; f=X^2-1 fails field input. LC17 supplies a primitive element only after L exists, whose degree is |G|.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: Finding certificates uniformly is not furnished by finite verification operations.

normalized_claim_cards.title: Product algebra boundary
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: Q^G with pointwise multiplication is equivariant, commutative, associative and unital with fixed constants Q, but is not a field for nontrivial G.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: G nontrivial for the failure; coordinate idempotents for distinct group elements.
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: Left regular coordinate translation preserves pointwise multiplication.
normalized_claim_cards.source_locator: paper/chapters01_03.tex: The regular representation supplies a model; paper/chapters07_08.tex: The multiplication carried by a normal basis
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: Distinct nonzero coordinate idempotents have product0. Conversely a finite-dimensional rational commutative associative unital algebra without zero divisors is a field: nonzero multiplication maps are injective and hence surjective.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: For trivial G the coordinate algebra is Q. Field multiplication and preservation must be established before Artin can apply.

normalized_claim_cards.title: Edition and appendix scope
normalized_claim_cards.normalized_statement: The edition records closed examples and operator statements, conditional arithmetic routes, bounded computation and dated external context; it asserts no uniform inverse Galois proof.
normalized_claim_cards.objects_and_hypotheses: The exact frozen manuscript, source contracts and computation records.
normalized_claim_cards.coefficient_domain: Domains separately stated in each source
normalized_claim_cards.action_and_variance: No finite-to-universal or model-to-arithmetic inference is made.
normalized_claim_cards.proof_check: Checked source-map locators LC16/17, computation bounds, basis conversion, deterministic reproduction commands, POSIX wrapper scope, and explicit distinctions of historical/current and math/layout evidence. Classical solvable/symmetric claims are named external inputs; M23 and Swan context are attributed outside elementary dependencies.
normalized_claim_cards.exceptional_or_boundary_cases: No whole historical manuscript re-audit; no external Belyi/Magma rerun; no independent Swan counterexample proof; no Lean certification; no global novelty or absence-of-later-paper certification.

external_source_leaves.title: Rational inverse Galois problem and dated status
exact_locators: Huang et al. v2, §1.1, printed pp.1–2
external_source_leaves.result_used: For each finite group G, seek a finite Galois field extension L/Q with Gal(L/Q) isomorphic to G. The general assertion remains open in the checked 2026 sources.
hypotheses: G is any finite abstract group; base is Q.

notation_dictionary.L: an actual field, finite over Q

external_source_leaves.application_check: A representation on a vector space, a G-action on a disconnected algebra, or a realization over a larger base is not by itself the requested field extension.
exceptions_or_caveats: This is a dated source check, not an exhaustive certification that no subsequent paper exists. The newer v2 status context was inspected on 9 October 2026.
external_source_leaves.coefficient_action_completion: Fields and finite groups as stated. No completion, grading, or analytic limit is supplied unless explicitly declared in the result.
external_source_leaves.project_implication: valid for the stated scope, subject to the manuscript separately supplying the listed hypotheses
external_source_leaves.classification: Conjectural or explicitly open in a checked source
external_source_leaves.proof_review_scope: Exact statement and application contract, not an independent reconstruction of the entire external proof.

external_source_leaves.title: Regular realization is a stronger input

external_source_leaves.title: Hilbert specialization with a controlled exceptional locus
exact_locators: Dèbes notes, Theorem 2.6.3(a),(d), printed p.85; Remark 2.6.5, p.87

external_source_leaves.source_status: proves theorem and corollary; modern paper states the regular consequence
external_source_leaves.result_used: Over Q, a finite Galois extension of Q(t_1,...,t_r) admits specializations retaining G on a Hilbert subset outside a proper Zariski closed exceptional locus. A fixed nonzero constraint polynomial may also be kept nonzero.
hypotheses: r ≥ 1; finite Galois field extension; a primitive polynomial for the full extension, not merely for an arbitrary smaller root field; localization avoids coefficients, denominators and discriminant zeros.

notation_dictionary.P: minimal polynomial of a primitive element of the entire Galois extension

external_source_leaves.application_check: The specialized primitive polynomial stays irreducible of degree |G|. Away from the model exceptional locus its splitting-field group embeds into G. exceptions_or_caveats: Characteristic zero alone is insufficient: Q is Hilbertian by the cited theorem; C is not.
For one parameter the excluded polynomial zero set is finite. In several parameters it is generally an infinite proper hypersurface.
Not every unbranched value retains the full group. Infinitely many suitable values need not, without a separate argument, describe distinct isomorphism classes for a nonregular constant extension.
For a nontrivial regular one-parameter extension, Huang et al. state infinitely many G-extensions over Q. The trivial group is handled separately.
The author lecture notes are a work in progress and have unfinished cross references. The locally pinned numbered statements, rather than dangling references, were used.

exact_locators: Theorem 4.28, p.69; Lemma 4.31 and Example 4.32, pp.70–71
external_source_leaves.result_used: Every S_n occurs over Q. Squarefree modular patterns, irreducibility, and an elementary permutation criterion provide a construction.

notation_dictionary.G_f: group of the splitting field, not of a single root field

external_source_leaves.application_check: The authors may prove their own subgroup criterion. The external arithmetic step is LC08. A full S_n splitting field has degree n!, not n.

Repeated low-degree factors must be excluded when making modular patterns.

external_source_leaves.title: Continuous finite quotients of the absolute Galois group
exact_locators: Theorem 7.13, statement on printed pp.125–126, especially (b) and (d)
external_source_leaves.result_used: Restriction Gal(Ω/F)→Gal(L/F) is a continuous surjection when L/F is a finite Galois intermediate extension. A continuous homomorphism q:Gal(Ω/F)→E to a finite discrete group has an open normal kernel H; M=Ω^H is finite Galois over F and Gal(M/F)≅Gal(Ω/F)/H≅im(q).
hypotheses: Ω/F is Galois and carries the Krull topology; E is finite with the discrete topology; q is a continuous group homomorphism. For the project take F=Q and Ω=Qbar.

notation_dictionary.q: the proposed lift to the finite group E
notation_dictionary.M=Ω^H: finite Galois field supplied by the correspondence

external_source_leaves.application_check: Chapter 6 has a continuous lift q with π∘q=ρ, where ρ is restriction to L. Then ker(q)⊆ker(ρ), so the order-reversing correspondence gives L⊆M. For a surjective lift, the identified group is E, and restriction to L becomes π; its kernel gives Gal(M/L)≅ker(π). The weak case supplies im(q), not necessarily E.
exceptions_or_caveats: An abstract homomorphism is insufficient without continuity. Openness follows from the finite discrete target and continuity, while normality follows from being a kernel.
This correspondence turns an already constructed continuous quotient into a finite field. It does not prove a proper lift exists for every embedding problem.
The first isomorphism theorem and the kernel inclusion are elementary project deductions, rather than extra existence theorems.

external_source_leaves.title: Primitive elements for finite characteristic-zero realizations
external_source_leaves.result_used: If E=F[α_1,...,α_r] is finite over F and α_2,...,α_r are separable over F, then E=F[γ] for some γ. In particular every finite separable field extension has a primitive element.
hypotheses: Finite field extension, with a finite generating list satisfying the separability condition; all algebraic generators are separable in characteristic zero. The project uses a finite Galois extension of Q.

notation_dictionary.γ: the primitive element used in the polynomial certificate
notation_dictionary.Q[γ]: the whole extension, not merely a subfield

external_source_leaves.application_check: The degree of the minimal polynomial of γ is [L:Q]=|G| for an existing G-realization. The power basis 1,γ,...,γ^(|G|−1) gives a unique rational expression for each automorphism image of γ, so the certificate format in Chapter 7 can encode any existing realization. These degree and basis assertions are the project’s elementary consequences of the source theorem.
exceptions_or_caveats: Existence of a primitive element for an already given finite separable extension is not a procedure to construct a realization of an arbitrary group.
No claim is made that a generator of an arbitrary smaller root field generates the full splitting field.
The source theorem is slightly stronger than the separable special case: its first generator need not be separable. Only the characteristic-zero special case is used.
